purpose: Test whether unequal standing genetic variation alone can make different pollinator-facing trait modules respond asynchronously under the same visitor environment, without changing the ecological selection operator.

trait_analogs.access: architecture-like functional matching axis; not literal corolla geometry
trait_analogs.investment: signal/display-like pollinator-facing investment axis; not literal colour

predeclared_contrasts.access_variation_effect: |access change| equal_high - |access change| access_constrained, averaged over left4/right4
predeclared_contrasts.investment_variation_effect: |investment change| equal_high - |investment change| investment_constrained, averaged over left4/right4

decision_rule.standing_variation_filter_supported_if: both predeclared deterministic contrasts are positive
decision_rule.next_step_if_supported: add trait-specific mutation supply/effect-size and cross-trait pleiotropic coupling in a separately frozen extension

claim_boundary: This pilot tests genetic availability, not literal molecular mechanisms.
Access is not asserted to equal flower shape and investment is not asserted to equal flower colour.
No claim is made that colour is universally easier to evolve than morphology.
Differences are induced experimentally by standing variation and therefore show possibility, not natural parameter values.
Mutation, linkage and pleiotropy remain absent in this pilot.
No natural island, time scale or evolutionary rate is calibrated.
